_comment: Connector-specific edits to GENERATED/authored files that a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and banned anti-patterns absent) and fails CI if a reprint dropped one. The factory regen for this connector lives in ~/Documents/Dev/cli-factory/threatdown (tooling/derive_spec.py builds the derived spec, tooling/apply_handfixes.py re-applies the generated-file edits).

handfixes.summary: The client-credentials token mint builds its default scope from a list (execute, read, write) joined with spaces, in both the client auto-mint and `auth login`. The wire value is unchanged: scope=execute read write. THREATDOWN_OAUTH_SCOPE still overrides it, split on whitespace.
handfixes.why: Press dogfood's oauth_scope_coverage scan reads the generated single string "execute read write" as one scope and reported 0/418 operations covered, failing shipcheck on a correct CLI. The list form lets the scan see each scope. Recorded by the build pane in .printing-press-patches/oauth-scope-list.json and re-applied after a cross-spec regenerate by cli-factory/threatdown/tooling/apply_handfixes.py; a reprint that skips that script reverts to resolveClientCredentialsScope() while go build and go test stay green.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Needs a press fix to the scope-coverage scan (split space-delimited scope literals); no spec extension can express it.

handfixes.summary: The root command's Short and Long help open with "ThreatDown OneView CLI" instead of the generated "Threatdown CLI".
handfixes.why: The press title-cases the API slug (threatdown -> Threatdown), which miscases the vendor brand on the first line of `threatdown-cli --help` and in the agent-context description. Applied at msp-skills onboarding (2026-10-14) to the stripped source; cli-factory/threatdown/tooling/apply_handfixes.py does not carry it, so a reprint reverts it unless this entry catches it.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: The derived spec already sets x-display-name "ThreatDown OneView"; the press should use it for the root help line instead of title-casing the slug.

handfixes.summary: Generated SKILL.md, AGENTS.md and guide.md (the source README) carry corrections for this CLI: the teach example passes --resource-type, the Claude Code MCP registration passes both OAuth env vars, the async-jobs section explains `respond --wait`, the respond verbs are documented as preview-until---confirm, and guide.md documents THREATDOWN_OAUTH_SCOPE and the client-secret prompt. SKILL.md and guide.md say the CLI requests a new token when the client or THREATDOWN_OAUTH_SCOPE changes and refuses to borrow another client's token (round 5, 2026-10-14), and SKILL.md's read-only line names endpoints diag-log.
handfixes.why: These files are re-rendered on every generate and re-vendored by onboard.py on every --resume. The generated text was wrong for this CLI: teach without --resource-type fails, `claude mcp add` with no --env gives an MCP server that 401s, and the generic `--dry-run` wording implied a preview the respond verbs do not give. Applied by cli-factory/threatdown/tooling/apply_handfixes.py (DOC_EDITS); a reprint that skips it ships the wrong instructions while every build gate stays green.

handfixes.summary: The respond verbs (isolate, restore, scan, reboot, update) print a target preview and send nothing without --confirm or the global --yes, and refuse more than --max-targets endpoints (default 25).
handfixes.why: This is the safety property governance.md, page.json and the README promise for the only commands that act on client machines by host name. The code is hand-written (respond_isolate.go is a novel file regen-merge keeps), but a reprint that regenerated the respond scaffold, or a refactor that flipped the default, would send jobs on a bare `respond isolate --host X` while the docs still say it previews. The asserts pin the preview note, the default cap and the refusal.

handfixes.summary: Secret-named JSON keys (as_uninstall_password, uninstall_password, password, secret, secret_hash, secret_token, token, custom_headers) are dropped at any depth before any row reaches the local store (generic blob, typed columns and FTS index, via the single mergeIncomingResourceData choke point), and an HTTP response that carries one is never written to the response cache. Helper: internal/cliutil/secretfields.go. The installers response (account-specific download links and signed URLs, no secret-named key) is also never cached (cliutil.IsSecretBearingPath) and never stored (mergeIncomingResourceData stores an empty object for the installers resource).
handfixes.why: Default `sync` pulls GET /v1/policies, whose every row carries as_uninstall_password (the tamper-protection password that uninstalls the ThreatDown agent), and GET /v1/notifications/subscriptions, whose rows carry the HMAC signing key secret_token; the generated store wrote both into data.db and resources_fts, and the response cache wrote GET bodies such as /v1/policies/{id}/secret to disk. Found at msp-skills onboarding (2026-10-14) by scanning the spec's 2xx response schemas for password/secret/token keys. A reprint regenerates store.go and client.go and silently drops both hooks while go build and go test stay green. internal/store/secret_fields_test.go proves both directions: with the hook reverted the sentinel lands in resources_fts. custom_headers was added after the round-1 adversarial review drove a webhook subscription whose custom_headers carried 'authorization: Bearer <sentinel>' into data.db, resources_fts and the response cache (the spec's example header key is authorization). installers was added after the round-3 adversarial review (2026-10-14) found `installers <account_id>` writing its signed url and link into the HTTP response cache while governance.md tiers it as credential-bearing; secret_fields_test.go upserts an installers row with a sentinel and fails with the guard reverted.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Needs a press feature: an x-secret / writeOnly-aware store projection that never persists credential fields; no spec extension expresses it today.

handfixes.summary: governance.md, README.md and page.json put every read whose output carries a credential in the Credential tier, not Read: every policies read (list/get/search/system-default/-v2/secret-get), sites secret, installation-tokens search, installers, webhooks and notifications list / get, and export of policies or notifications (export has no webhooks resource). governance.md also names the MCP read-only mode's GET gap. `export` is not listed as a blanket Read command.
handfixes.why: The generated governance tiers by verb, so 'every list / get / search' was Read and an agent policy keyed on it would let an agent read every customer's tamper-protection password. Applied at msp-skills onboarding (2026-10-14); these files are preserved across onboard --resume but a fleet re-mint or a hand rewrite can drop the carve-out. Round-2 review (2026-10-14) found `export policies` / `export notifications` dumping uninstall passwords and signing keys while `export` was named in the Read row. Round-3 review (2026-10-14) found `export` cannot export webhooks, so the wording names policies and notifications only.

handfixes.summary: Every variable the binaries read is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb user_config + server.mcp_config.env), server.json (MCP Registry) and the three mcp-install.md env blocks. Beyond the client id and secret these are the optional THREATDOWN_OAUTH_SCOPE, THREATDOWN_BASE_URL, THREATDOWN_TOKEN_URL, THREATDOWN_USER_AGENT, THREATDOWN_MCP_READ_ONLY, THREATDOWN_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN and PRINTING_PRESS_CLIENT_PROFILE, blank (not placeholders) in mcp-install.md.
handfixes.why: check_env_schema failed the onboard with 7 read-but-undeclared variables, so a Claude Desktop install could never set read-only mode or a reduced scope. onboard.py --resume re-vendors manifest.json from the press source, which declares only the two credentials, so a re-onboard drops the other seven while the build stays green (check_env_schema would then catch it; this entry names the cause). Applied at msp-skills onboarding 2026-10-14.

handfixes.summary: Every documented `threatdown-mcp --transport http` launch (README ChatGPT line and FAQ, mcp-install.md remote section) sets THREATDOWN_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN and says callers send it as Authorization: Bearer.
handfixes.why: The scaffolded docs launched `threatdown-mcp --transport http` with only the OAuth credentials; the binary exits 1 with 'THREATDOWN_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN must be set to a non-empty bearer token before starting --transport http' (measured 2026-10-14), so the documented ChatGPT/remote path never started. check_install_docs does not check the token, so nothing gates this.

handfixes.summary: doctor reports an ERROR api verdict (and an ERROR credentials verdict) when the OneView account probe GET /v1/info/account returns 404, instead of 'reachable (HTTP 404 at /)' and a WARN.
handfixes.why: check_doctor_truth (CI hard gate, issue #282) failed the onboard: a THREATDOWN_BASE_URL that is not the OneView API root made doctor report the API as healthy. Generated doctor.go has no doctorUnexpectedStatus/doctorWrongBaseURL (the fleet's hand-wired fix), so a reprint reverts this; the gate would then fail again. Applied at msp-skills onboarding 2026-10-14.

asserts.contains: base_url is not the OneView API root. Point THREATDOWN_BASE_URL at https://api.threatdown.com/oneview or unset it, and check base_url in the file named by config_path.

handfixes.summary: An env-sourced THREATDOWN_BASE_URL or THREATDOWN_TOKEN_URL is marked as an env override in config.Load and configForSave writes the file's own value back instead, so config.toml never captures the override and unsetting the variable restores the default on the next run.
handfixes.why: The generated configForSave restored only env-sourced ClientID/ClientSecret, so the first token mint (auth login, doctor or any MCP tool call) wrote the env base_url and token_url into config.toml. After that, unsetting the variable had no effect: requests kept going to the old base URL and every new mint sent the client ID and secret to the old token host. The doctor hint ('or unset it'), the manifest's 'leave blank for the default' and governance.md's 'override' were all false after one use. Found by the round-3 adversarial review (2026-10-14); a reprint regenerates config.go and silently reverts it while go build and go test stay green. internal/config/env_urls_test.go fails with the restore lines removed.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Generator defect (66 of 68 fleet configs behave the same): configForSave should restore every env-overridden field, not only credentials.

handfixes.summary: governance.md's tier tables name every non-GET write command in the binary (job issue and cancel, policy -v2 writes, group assignment, alert routing, email-protection, imports, every delete) plus endpoints diag-log, and state the rule for anything missing: a POST, PUT or DELETE pp:method that is not a search, export or report query is Security config at minimum. README.md and page.json carry the same Endpoint actions list.
handfixes.why: The generated governance tiers by keyword, and the round-3 adversarial review (2026-10-14) enumerated 310 non-GET commands from agent-context and found dozens in no tier (notifications change-owner / remove-email can silence alerting; groups assign-endpoints moves machines across policies). governance.md is preserved across onboard --resume, but a fleet re-mint or a hand rewrite can shrink the tables back to examples.

asserts.contains: The tables name every write command in this release.

handfixes.summary: A client-credentials token is saved with token_binding, a fingerprint of the client ID, scope and token URL it was minted for (config.TokenBindingFor). tokenBoundElsewhere is true when the current process's client ID, THREATDOWN_OAUTH_SCOPE or token URL give a different fingerprint, or the token is unbound (auth set-token) while client credentials are configured; then the client mints its own token, and when it has no secret to mint with, authHeader returns an error instead of the cached token. validateCachedRequestAuth resolves the token first so a response cached under another client's token is never served. resolveClientCredentials trims like auth login. auth login records the binding, auth set-token clears it. Round 6 (2026-10-14): the refusal is the typed client.ErrTokenBoundElsewhere, which exits with the auth code 4 and which doctor reports as a credentials error (the API is not probed); an unbound token yields to a client ID or a secret (either one); and config.Load never pairs an environment client ID with the secret saved for a different client in credentials.toml. Round 7 (2026-10-14): auth login given either flag saves the exact client pair it minted with, and save() keeps the saved pair in its snapshot so a second mint in one process (tail --follow, a long sync) does not write it back empty.
handfixes.why: Found by the round-4 adversarial review and the Codex branch review (2026-10-14). Every process run as the same OS user shares one credentials.toml, and the generated needsClientCredentialsMint checked only token presence and expiry. So an MCP server configured with a separate read-only OAuth client (and THREATDOWN_OAUTH_SCOPE=read) reused the admin's cached execute token and issued an isolation job through threatdown_execute, with no token request of its own; the README's 'the CLI can only do what that client is permitted to do' was false. A reprint regenerates client.go, config.go, credentials.go and auth.go and silently reverts this while go build and go test stay green. Round 5 (adversarial + Codex, 2026-10-14) found the first version failed open: a process with a client ID but no secret, or only THREATDOWN_OAUTH_SCOPE set, still used the admin token; a GET cache hit (keyed on the cached token) served the other client's data before authHeader ran; and an unbound token outranked configured credentials. internal/client/token_binding_test.go (both tests) fails with any of these guards removed.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Generator defect: the press's client-credentials cache should key the token on the client ID and scope.

handfixes.summary: endpoints diag-log (a GET that makes the endpoint generate a diagnostic log) is marked Mutating in the MCP code-orchestration table, so THREATDOWN_MCP_READ_ONLY=1 refuses it through threatdown_execute; the CLI command no longer carries mcp:read-only; and its signed download URL is never written to the HTTP response cache (IsSecretBearingPath), so every call reaches the endpoint.
handfixes.why: Found by the round-4 adversarial review and the Codex branch review (2026-10-14). The generated read-only gate allowed every GET, so a 'reporting agent' MCP server could make client endpoints generate logs, which governance.md tiers as an Endpoint action. The response is a signed S3 URL that was cached at rest and served on a repeat call without asking the endpoint again. code_orch.go, endpoints_diag-log.go and secretfields' caller are regenerated on a reprint; TestCodeOrchExecuteReadOnlyRefusesNonGET in code_orch_writebody_test.go fails if diag-log stops being refused.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Needs a spec extension the press honors for side-effecting GETs (mark the operation mutating) so the gate, cache bypass and MCP hint follow by construction.

handfixes.summary: tail strips the secret fields (as_uninstall_password, secret_token, custom_headers and the rest of secretFieldKeys) from every polled response before streaming it, and is hidden from the MCP server (mcp:hidden).
handfixes.why: Found by the round-4 adversarial review and the Codex branch review (2026-10-14). tail policies and tail notifications streamed every policy's uninstall password and every subscription's signing key and auth headers, while the MCP tail tool advertised readOnlyHint=true and stayed enabled under THREATDOWN_MCP_READ_ONLY=1: the twin of the round-2 export finding. As an MCP tool tail also never returned (the MCP argv builder drops follow:false, so the poll loop ran forever). A reprint regenerates tail.go; internal/cli/tail_secrets_test.go fails with the redaction removed.

handfixes.summary: manifest.json, server.json and the --client-profile flag help say PRINTING_PRESS_CLIENT_PROFILE is not enforced by this connector and does not limit which sites a call reaches, instead of promising a tenant-bound MCP server.
handfixes.why: Found by the round-4 adversarial review and the Codex branch review (2026-10-14). No ThreatDown platform adapter is registered (registerPlatformSource is never called), so BindMCPServerProfile and VerifyMCPInvocation return without gating and a profile set for customer isolation silently reached every site. The variable stays declared because the binary reads it (check_env_schema). Wiring a real tenant gate is a per-vendor design task; the honest fix is the wording. manifest.json and server.json are re-vendored on every onboard --resume and root.go on a reprint.

handfixes.summary: respond pending treats a job search the server did not end with an empty next_cursor (page cap reached, or no cursor confirmation) as incomplete: human output warns and drops the all-clear, and the all-clear itself names what it checked (waiting, timed out, expired, failed; cancelled jobs are not listed). fleet stale applies the same unconfirmed-end rule to its stale and --twins searches, and the respond pending all-clear names any --command / --site filter.
handfixes.why: Found by the Codex branch review (2026-10-14): view.Truncated reached the JSON output but the table path ignored it, so a scan that hit the page cap could print an all-clear while older failed jobs went unchecked. respond_pending.go is a hand-written novel file; this entry pins the guard against a refactor. Codex round 2 added: a missing next_cursor ended the scan without marking it incomplete, and the old all-clear ('Every job ... completed') counted cancelled jobs as completed. Round 6 found the fleet stale twin (it printed 'No endpoints unseen' after an unconfirmed end) and the filtered all-clear reading as fleet-wide.

asserts.not_contains: Every job in the last %s completed

handfixes.summary: The fleet reports (fleet stale, fleet health, customer report, respond pending, threats spread) pass tdMaxAge(cmd) to their local-copy staleness hints: an explicit global --max-age (0 disables) wins, else 24h.
handfixes.why: Found by the Codex branch review round 3 (2026-10-14): the hints hard-coded 24h while printing 'older than --max-age=24h0m0s', so --max-age 1m never warned and --max-age 0 never disabled them. These are hand-written novel files; internal/cli/td_max_age_test.go pins the flag handling.

handfixes.summary: customer report resolves its site argument by exact id or account_id first, then by name; two sites with the same exact name are ambiguous (listed with their ids) instead of a silent first pick, and a site named like another site's id never shadows it.
handfixes.why: Found by the Codex branch review round 3 (2026-10-14): matchSite returned the first exact name match, so duplicate customer names (common across MSP sub-accounts) silently reported on the wrong customer. TestMatchSite in threatdown_fleet_test.go fails on the old resolver.

asserts.contains: duplicate exact names should be ambiguous

handfixes.summary: `golang.org/x/text` is pinned at v0.41.0, above the fixes for GO-2026-5970 and GO-2026-6629
handfixes.why: Press 4.33.5 emits `golang.org/x/text v0.39.0` as an indirect dependency. osv-scanner flags v0.39.0 for GO-2026-6629 (a panic parsing crafted input in x/text/secure/precis). The repo security gate tracks it, and a reprint from a press that still emits v0.39.0 would quietly bring it back. Bumped with `go get golang.org/x/text@v0.41.0` + `go mod tidy`; build and tests pass.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Raise the golang.org/x/text floor in the press module template so generated go.mod files ship at v0.41.0 or later by construction.
